                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptance of that Saviour, and way of Salvation, which G<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d hath revealed in it for lost sinners; and that Holiness of Life which God hath made necessary to it.</ns0:note>, which the Son of man shall give unto you <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">All which (saith he) I, who am <ns0:hi>the Son of man</ns0:hi> (a name he ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />narily giveth to himse f) will give unto you freely: Not that you are to do nothing; no, labour for it; tho it be a <ns0:hi>gift,</ns0:hi> yet it is a gift upon Labour, for all your Labour will not procure it; there will be a great deal of Free Grace seen when you have given all diligence</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 3.17. and 17.5. Mark 1.11. and 9.7. Luke 2.22. and 9.35. Chap. 1.33. and 5.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. and 8.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>8. 2 Pet. 1.17.</ns0:note> for him hath God the Father sealed <ns0:note n="w:" place="bottom">And Christ must give it; for the Father, in whose hand this Life is, hath (as men by their Seals use to confirm the Commi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sions they give out to any persons to do any thing for them, and in their Name) confirmed Christ as his Commissioner, to give out this Eternal Life to whomsoever he pleaseth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Then said they unto him, VVhat shall we do that we might work the works of God <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">They easily understood that our Saviour did not speak of any Worldly Food, by his opposing the Labour he men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioneth, and persuadeth for, to a labour for the World; but still they did not understand what Labour he spake of, but dreamt of the <ns0:hi>works of the Law</ns0:hi>; knowing of no other work which God commanded, but what was pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />scribed in the Law; and they (probably) being some, or many of them strict Observers (especially of the Law con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained in Ordinances) and probably, many of them of the Moral Law also, according to the sense of it given by their Teachers; in which sense the Young man, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 19.20. being bid by our Saviour, keep the Law; and naming most of the Precepts of the Second Table, told him, <ns0:hi>All these things have I kept from my Youth: what lack I <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>et?</ns0:hi> They wondred what works our Saviour meant; what Labour, when he said, <ns0:hi>Labour for that Bread,</ns0:hi> or that meat <ns0:hi>which endureth to Eternal<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Life.</ns0:hi> Thinking that those which kept the Law (in the sense before expressed) had no more to do.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Jesus answered and said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 3, 23.</ns0:note> This is the work of God, that you believe on him whom he hath sent <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Our Lord calleth them to a work they never thought of: The owning, and acknowledgment of him to be the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; the embracing and receiving him as such, and trusting <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>im with all the concerns of their Souls; which was necessary, notwithstanding all their Acts of Obedience to the Law, tho most certainly productive also of that Obedience, and inseparable from it. This our Saviour calleth, The <ns0:hi>work of God,</ns0:hi> in answer to what they had said about working the works of God. Yet this will not prove that we are Justified by Works, because we are Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stified by Faith; for here is no Discourse concerning the causation of Faith in the Justification of a Soul, but onely concerning what is the Will of God, as to all those that shall be saved.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 They <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>aid therefore unto him, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 16.1. 1 Co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 1.22.</ns0:note> What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee? VVhat dost thou work <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">They thought it reasonable, that he who brought forth a new Doctrine into the World (such as Faith in him was, they having never heard any such thing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> from their Doctors the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi>) should confirm his Mission by some Miraculous Operation. But this was a strange stupidity, considering the Sign he had so lately shewed them, of feeding <ns0:hi>five thousand</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>five loaves</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>two fishes.</ns0:hi> So it was manifest they sought for a Sign, not to promove or confirm their Faith, but merely to feed their C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>riosity; and what our Saviour said, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 12.39. <ns0:hi>A wicked and Adulterous Generation seeketh after a Sign,</ns0:hi> was <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plicable to them; and those words, <ns0:hi>believe thee,</ns0:hi> emin<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tly confirm it; for the aforesaid Miracle speaking in <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>m a <ns0:hi>Creative Power,</ns0:hi> and being such as was never wroug<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t by any Creature, they were obliged to believe him, wi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hout any further Sign. God ought to be believed upon his bare word.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:341" />31 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 10.3.</ns0:note> Our Fathers did eat Manna in the desart; as it is written, He gave them bread from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven to eat <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Here they magnifie <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>; he did not bring them a Law onely, but confirmed it by Signs from Heaven, to be the Will of God, by obtaining for them Bread to be rained from Heaven to satisfie their Hunger, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 16.15. <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 11.7. which is also confirmed by the <ns0:hi>Psalmist, Psal.</ns0:hi> 78.25. This <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> did for the whole Congregation of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> forty Years together. From hence they would seem to conclude, That they had more ground to believe <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> than Christ; who, tho he had indeed lately fed five thousand with five Loaves, yet had done no such thing. Not con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sidering that <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> in what he did, was but an Instrument to obtain of God by Prayer such a Miracle, for supporting his People in the Wilderness; and that what he had done, was done by a Creating Power inherent in himself, by which he multiplyed that little proportion of Bread which they had, to make it sufficient to feed such a quantity as five thousand, besides Women and Children; to which effect it bare no proportion.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">You are mistaken in your Opinion of that <ns0:hi>Manna,</ns0:hi> which indeed was Bread from Heaven; <ns0:hi>Spiritual meat</ns0:hi> (as the Apostle calleth it, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.3.) But it was not given you by any Power or Vertue in or from <ns0:hi>Moses; Moses</ns0:hi> said other<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise; when it was first rained down, he told them, <ns0:hi>This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat, Exod.</ns0:hi> 16.15. It was the Lord, not <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> that gave you that Bread</ns0:note>; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven <ns0:note n="c:" place="bottom">Nor was that <ns0:hi>true Spiritual bread</ns0:hi>; it was onely Spiritual (as the Apostle calleth it) because it was <ns0:hi>Typical,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />figurative</ns0:hi> of me. My Father giveth you <ns0:hi>the true Bread from Heaven</ns0:hi>: It was he that gave your Fathers <ns0:hi>Manna,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>; and it is he who giveth you <ns0:hi>me,</ns0:hi> who am the <ns0:hi>true bread,</ns0:hi> of which that bread was but Typical, a sha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dow, and a Figure.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> gave you Spiritual, Heavenly Bread; but that was onely Spiritual, as it was Typical and prefigured me; Heavenly, as it came from the lower Heavens, was rained down from thence; not made upon the Earth by the Art of man, and was therefore called the Bread of Angels; but I am the <ns0:hi>true bread of God,</ns0:hi> signified by that Type, who came not down from the lower, but from the highest Heavens; and who do not only maintain, and uphold Life in men (as that did) but give Life to men; and that not a mere Natural Life, but a Spiritual and Eternal Life; and that not to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> onely, for whose <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> alone <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> was, but <ns0:hi>to the World.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Most Interpreters agree, that they spake this seriously; that is, that they were willing enough to have such Bread, (if any such were to be had); but yet not conceiving aright the Nature and Excellency of the Bread our Saviour men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned; and this occasioned his clear explication of it in the following Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Bread that giveth Spiritual and Eternal Life, and the Bread that upholdeth and maintaineth Spiritual Life. The <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> whom God hath sent into the World, to quicken those that are dead in Trespasses and Sins, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.1. And <ns0:hi>to give Eternal Life to as many as the Father hath given me</ns0:hi>: But those that have this Life, must <ns0:hi>come unto me</ns0:hi>; which he Interprets in the next Phrase by <ns0:hi>believing in him</ns0:hi>: Thus he taketh them off all gross and Carnal Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptions of eating and drinking in a Carnal manner; and minds them to think of getting and maintaining another kind of Life than they dreamt of. By believing in him, we have formerly shewed is to be understood a receiving of him as the <ns0:hi>Mediator</ns0:hi> and Saviour of men, and closing with him, and committing their Souls in all their Spiritual con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerns unto him;</ns0:note>; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.14. and 7.37.</ns0:note> He that cometh to me, shall never hunger, and he that believeth on me, shall never thirst <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">and he that doth so (saith he) shall ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver <ns0:hi>hunger</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>thirst</ns0:hi>: That is, shall never want any thing necessary for him for <ns0:hi>Life and Eternal Happiness.</ns0:hi> And for things of this Life, he shall have Food convenient for him; he shall <ns0:hi>be fed,</ns0:hi> Psal. 37.3. See such a Promise, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 49. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 But I said unto you, that ye also have seen me, and believe not <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">You have seen me in the Flesh, you have heard my Doctrine, you have seen the Miracles which I have wrought, confirming that Doctrine, and me to be the true <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi>; for I have done amongst you those works which never any man did: But you are of the Generation of those of whom it was Prophesied, That in seeing, you shou'd not see, nor yet perceive; for tho you have <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>een me with your Bodily Eyes, and could not but <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> by what works I have done, that I am the true <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; yet you do not own and acknowledge me as such, nor will by Faith close with me, and come unto me for Life and Happiness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 All that the Father giveth me <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Here ariseth a great Question amongst Interpreters of various persuasions, What <ns0:hi>giving of the Father</ns0:hi> is here meant; whether <ns0:hi>an eternal designation of Persons to eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Life</ns0:hi>; in order to the obtaining of which, the Persons so Predestinated are given to Christ, as he who was to be the <ns0:hi>Messiah, Saviour,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Redeemer</ns0:hi> of the World: Or the infusing the habits of special saving Grace; by which Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons are enabled actually to believe. If the former, the words do not onely infer an infallible connexion betwixt Faith, and Eternal Life and Salvation; but also betwixt the Decree of Election, and the collation of special Grace; by which men are enabled to believe, and believing, are saved. That which seemeth to favou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the latter Opinion, is, that the <ns0:hi>Verb</ns0:hi> is in the Present Tense: It is not, all <ns0:hi>that the Father hath given,</ns0:hi> but all that the <ns0:hi>Father giveth</ns0:hi>; which would incline us to think, that tho in other Texts the Fathers giving of Souls to Christ may signifie his <ns0:hi>Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Election</ns0:hi>; yet in this Text it rather signifieth the do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nation, or giving the habits of Special Grace. But there are very Learned and Pious Interpreters of another mind; who think by the <ns0:hi>Fathers giving,</ns0:hi> is meant the Fathers <ns0:hi>chusing Souls in him,</ns0:hi> Ephes. 1.4. Certain it is, that there are some chosen to Life, and the certain means by which that Life is to be obtained, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 1.4, 5. And as certain it is, that Persons so chosen in him, shall neither miss of that Life, nor yet of that effectual means by which it shall be obtained. Whether that <ns0:hi>Eternal Election,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Donation,</ns0:hi> be here intended or no, is not so momentous to deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine. For the <ns0:hi>Iesuits</ns0:hi> Argument, That if we understand it of such an <ns0:hi>Eternal gift</ns0:hi>; our Saviour rather excuseth, than accuseth them for their unbelief, by telling them they could not believe, because they were not given unto him; it holdeth as strong against <ns0:hi>Special Grace,</ns0:hi> as against <ns0:hi>parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular Election</ns0:hi>; so as if that were true, it could be Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preted in neither of those senses; but by their leaves it doth not at all excuse them, unless they did what in them lay to come to Christ, (but this Question belongs rather to <ns0:hi>Po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lemical Writers,</ns0:hi> than Interpreters.) Certain it is, that it is such a giving here mentioned, as shall be followed by a coming to Christ; that is, <ns0:hi>believing in him,</ns0:hi> and by a true Faith receiving of him;</ns0:note>, shall come to me: and him that cometh to me, I will in no wise cast out <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">and those that do so, our Lord saith, he will in no wise cast out. Out of Heaven, say some; others understand it of perseverance; but certainly the Phrase denoteth no more than the freeness and readi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of Christ to receive every one who truly believeth in him, and to preserve him to Eternal Life and Salvation. Who they are that are given to Christ, and that will, or shall believe in him, is a Secret that is known unto God alone: But this may be known to all, that Christ will not throw off any Soul that is willing to <ns0:hi>receive him</ns0:hi> as its Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour; and that no such Soul shall perish for ever.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 For I came down from Heaven, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 26.39. Chap. 5.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Our Lord confirmeth what he had before said con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning his Gracious Reception of Believers, and preserving them by his Grace in their state of Grace; so that they shall not be cast out with Reprobates in the day of Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment; from this, That he came not to execute any par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular will of his own, but what was also the will of his Father, who sent him into the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And this is the Fathers will which hath sent me, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.28. and 17.12. and 18.9.</ns0:note> That of all which he hath given me, I should lose nothing <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">For this he revealeth to be his Fathers will, that <ns0:hi>of all his Father had given him, he should lose none</ns0:hi>; where by the Fathers <ns0:hi>giving</ns0:hi> must be meant, either his Eternal Act (having chosen some to Eternal Life) in giving them to his Son, for the work of their Redemption; or, which is but the effect and product of that, the working, preser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving, and upholding in them those Habits and Exercises of Grace, by which that Eternal Life is to be obtained. Our Lord declareth it to be the will of his Father, That he should not suffer any of these to miscarry;</ns0:note>, but should raise it up again at the last day <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">but tho their Bodies dye and turn into dust, yet Christ at the last day should come to raise the Dead, and in particular, raise them up; not that they onely shall rise, (for how then shall all appear before the Judgment-seat of God, to receive ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to what they have done in the Flesh?) but they are those alone who shall receive any benefit by the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection; and therefore they are called the Children of the <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi>; and the Resurrection is sometimes spoken of in Scripture as if it were to be peculiar to them, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.11. By this the certainty of the Resurrection is established; it being asserted, as the effect of the <ns0:hi>will of God,</ns0:hi> which none hath resisted at any time.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:341" />40 And this is the will of him that sent me, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.16. and 4.14. and ver. 27, 54.</ns0:note> that every one which seeth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Our Lord having asserted the will of God, as to the final issue and happiness of Believers, goes on to assert the means by which in this Life using, they must obtain this Life; those are <ns0:hi>seeing the Son,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>believing in him</ns0:hi>; see<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing him, not with the Eyes of their Bodies; or seeing his Miraculous Operations, both which these <ns0:hi>Capernaites</ns0:hi> did, and yet did not believe, (as he told them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 36.) but a seeing them with the Eye of their Minds, discerning him as the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and Saviour of the World: So seeing him, as to believe on him; as to these, he confirmeth it again to be the will of his Father, that they should live Eternally,</ns0:note> the Son, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieveth on him, may have everlasting life <ns0:hi>p:</ns0:hi> and I will raise him up at the last day <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">and that they should be raised again at the last day; and that by him, whom God had ordained to be the <ns0:hi>Iudge both of the quick and the dead,</ns0:hi> Acts 10.42. which agreeth with what he had before said, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 5.28.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 The Jews then murmured at him <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were exceeding prone to this sin of mur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />muring, which is a complaining either through Indigna<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, or impatience of what men hear spoken, or see done; the thing which offended, seemeth not to be his calling him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self the <ns0:hi>true bread,</ns0:hi> and the bread of Life; but because he said, that he came down from Heaven.</ns0:note>, because he said, I am the bread which came down from Heaven.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And they said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 13.55. Mark 6.3. Luke 4.22.</ns0:note> Is not this Jesus the Son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How is it then that he saith, I came down from Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">For <ns0:hi>Capernaum,</ns0:hi> where our Saviour now was, was not far from <ns0:hi>Nazareth,</ns0:hi> where he had been Educated, and Lived near Thirty Years with <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi> his reputed Father. Understanding therefore nothing of our Saviours Miracu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lous Conception by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost in the Womb of the Virgin; they were much offended at his Discourse of his coming down from Heaven.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 Jesus therefore answered, and said unto them, Murmure not among your selves <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">By this our Saviour gives them another Proof of his Divine Nature, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> in his knowing of their Hearts and Thoughts; for tho they were inwardly angry, and in a rage, yet we read not of any words spoken by them; but our Saviour needed not their words to tell him what was in the secret of their Hearts. Our Saviour bids them not murmure at this, for he had much more than this to tell them, as followeth.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Cant. 1.4. Ver. 65.</ns0:note> No man can come unto me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">That by <ns0:hi>drawing</ns0:hi> here, is not to be understood any <ns0:hi>coaction,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>force</ns0:hi> upon the <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> is a thing on all hands out of Question; but whether by it be onely to be understood a <ns0:hi>rational drawing</ns0:hi> by Arguments (used in the Ministry of the Gospel) or a further powerful Influence upon the Soul, inclining it to be willing and obedient, that is the Question. The Patrons of a power in mans will to do what is Spiritu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally good and necessary in order to Eternal <ns0:hi>Life</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Salva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion,</ns0:hi> understand it of the former onely (of which the <ns0:hi>compelling,</ns0:hi> mentioned <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 14.23. is to be understood, (for the Ministers of the Gospel have no other Power to compel); but in regard the drawing here mentioned is the Acts not of the Servants, but of the Master; not of the Ministers, but of the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi>; it is more reasonably con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluded that it here signifies a Divine Power put forth upon the Soul of man, by which it is made Obedient to the Heavenly Call, and willing to close with the offer of Christ in the Gospel; for tho no such thing can necessarily be con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cluded from the word <ns0:hi>draw,</ns0:hi> yet it is easily concluded from the Nature of the motion, in coming to Christ, which is the Souls motion to a sublime Spiritual Object, to which no Soul hath any power of it self; such is the darkness of the Humane Mind, the obstinacy of the Will, the deprava<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Affections, unless it be Illuminated and drawn by the Spirit of God. No Soul is able of it self to discern Spiritual things, so as to see that Goodness and Excellency that is in them, much less to move towards the participa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of them.</ns0:note>, and I will raise him up at the last day.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 31.34. Heb. 8.10. and 10.16.</ns0:note> It is written in the Prophets <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Either in <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 54.13. or in the Book of the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets; for tho the words be to be found onely in <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> yet words of the same import are also to be found in <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />remiah, Ezekiel, Ioel,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Micah.</ns0:hi> All they whom the Lord hath chosen, shall be taught of God</ns0:note>, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me <ns0:note n="x:" place="bottom">Therefore (saith he) said I to you, <ns0:hi>Every man that hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour proveth the Doctrine which he had delivered to them, from the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets; not because their Authority was greater than his, or in any degree equal with his; but because the Prophets and their Writings were in greater Authority and Reputa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion with them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  </ns0:note> Your fathers did eat Manna in the wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derness, and are dead <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">and they are Naturally dead<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> (<ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> would not always preserve their Natural Life) and those of them who were <ns0:hi>unbelievers,</ns0:hi> are also dead <ns0:hi>eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nally</ns0:hi>; their eating of <ns0:hi>Manna,</ns0:hi> which was a Type of me, without believing in me, would not save them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 51, 58.</ns0:note> This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">But I am that Bread of Life, who came out of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ighest Heavens, from the bosom of my Father; that Bread which if a man <ns0:hi>eateth</ns0:hi> thereof, he shall never dye eternally. Eating Christ in this Text signifieth no more than believing in him, so often before mentioned under the Notion of <ns0:hi>coming to him, believing in him,</ns0:hi> &c. And be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving is fitly expressed by this Notion of <ns0:hi>Eating</ns0:hi>; because as eating is the application of Meat to our Stomacks, for the sustenance of our Bodily Life; so believing is the ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plication of Christ to the Soul, for the beginning and in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crease of Spiritual Life, and at last obtaining Life Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 I am the living bread, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.13.</ns0:note> which came down from heaven <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 33, & 35. Our Saviour's so often inculcating this, and what follows, lets us see both how ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessary this is to be known, and also how difficult the work of believing is</ns0:note>. If any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever <ns0:note n="e." place="bottom">Those words, <ns0:hi>he shall live for ever,</ns0:hi> ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pound those that went before in the 50<ns0:hi>th.</ns0:hi> Verse, <ns0:hi>that a man might eat thereof and not dye</ns0:hi>

                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>

               <ns0:p n="52">52 The Jews therefore strove amongst them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.9.</ns0:note> How can this man give us <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> flesh to eat <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">They will still understand Spiritual things in a Carnal sense; yet it is hard to conceive how they could imagine that Christ spake of giving them his Flesh to eat, as men eat the flesh of Oxen or Sheep; but which way soever they did understand it indeed, their captious temper inclined them to conceal any other sense they had of it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and to re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />present what our Saviour said, as exceeding absurd.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily I say unto you, Except <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>t. 26.26, 28.</ns0:note> ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The short and true sense of these words is, that with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out a true believing in the Lord Jesus Christ, as he who dyed for our sins; no man hath any thing in him of true Spiritual Life, nor shall ever come to Eternal Life. Here are two Questions arise from this Verse and what follows. 1. <ns0:hi>Whether the flesh of Christ, that is, his Humane Nature, giveth Life</ns0:hi>? or all <ns0:hi>our Life floweth from the Divine Nature?</ns0:hi> That is a Question betwixt the <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Calvi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nists</ns0:hi>; the former affirming, that there is a quickning ver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tue in the Humane Nature of Christ by vertue of its Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sonal Union with the Divine Nature. It is a curious Question, serving to no great E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ification; those who have <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap> mind to be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap> in it, and to read what is said on <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> side, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> read <ns0:hi>Tarnovius</ns0:hi> on this Text, and <ns0:hi>Zanchy,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">

                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> betwixt the Papists and us, Whether this and the fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />l<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="4 letters">

                     </ns0:gap>g Verses sp<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>ke any thing about the eating of the <ns0:hi>flesh, and drinking the blood of Christ in the Sacrament.</ns0:hi> All <ns0:hi>Protestants</ns0:hi> deny it, both <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Calvinists.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> most absurdly affirm it, to maintain their most ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />surd D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ctrine of <ns0:hi>Trans<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>tantiation.</ns0:hi> The vanity of their <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, as to this Text, appears, 1. Because it was a year and upwards after this before the Sacrament of the Lords Supper was Instituted; and it is very absurd to think that our Saviour should speak of an Institution not in being; his Doctrine about it being what it was impossible People should understand. Nor, Secondly, is the Proposition true, of <ns0:hi>Sacramental eating</ns0:hi>; for many m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>lesh, and drank the Blood of Christ, and yet be Spiritually alive, and be saved eternally. Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sides that mere Sacramental eating the Flesh, and drinking the Blood of Christ, will not give Life. But the <ns0:hi>eating</ns0:hi> here spoken of, giveth Life, Eternal Life, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 56, 58. 3. Besides, it is plain from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29. That the <ns0:hi>eating</ns0:hi> here spoken of, is believing<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but it is plain, that <ns0:hi>eating the Flesh,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>drink<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Blood of Christ in the Sacrament,</ns0:hi> is not <ns0:hi>believing.</ns0:hi> By all which it is apparent that our Saviour saith nothing in this Text of a Sacramental eating the Flesh, and drinking the Blood of Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:342" />54 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.14.</ns0:note> Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ernal life <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">He hath it in a sure and just right Title; and he shall have it in a certain Actual Possession:</ns0:note>: and I will raise him up at the last day <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And in order to it, he shall have a joyful Resurrection unto it at the last day. This is no more than what our Saviour had often said, par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticularly <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.18, 36. admitting what was before said, that by eating the Flesh, and drinking the Blood of Christ, is to be meant b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>lievin<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> in him; onely here is a clearer dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />covery than was there of the true object of that Faith which justifieth, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Christ Crucified,</ns0:hi> for that is signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fied by the <ns0:hi>Flesh and Blood mentioned.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">I as a Christ Crucified, not merely considered as to my Divine Nature, but as to both Natures united in one Person, and particularly, with respect to my death and suffering, am indeed the Food of Souls; not a Typical Food, as <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> was, but a true and real Food, which nourisheth them to Eternal Life; and the most excellent Food for them. In which sense Christ is called, <ns0:hi>The true Light, Chap.</ns0:hi> 1.9. and the <ns0:hi>true Vine, Chap.</ns0:hi> 15.1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="56">56 He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">He that acknowledgeth and receiveth me, tho he seeth me as a Man, consisting of Flesh and Blood, and that par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticularly applyeth himself to me as dying for the sins of the World; and committeth his Soul in all its concerns for Life and Salvation to me,</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>abideth. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> dwelleth in me, and I in him <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">is united to me, and I to him: He is united to me by Faith and Love, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 3.17. 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3.23, 24. and 4.16. And I am united to him by a mutual Love, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.23. and by my Holy Spirit, As our <ns0:hi>Bread</ns0:hi> and Meat, which we are nourished by, doth not dwell in us, and nourish, unless we eat it: So neither doth Christ do good to any Soul, unless such a Soul as by Faith receiveth him, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieveth in him. Wh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t is said in this Verse maketh it evi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dent, that these Verses cannot be understood of any Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cramental eating, for it is not true, That Christ dwelleth in every Soul, or that every Soul dwelleth and abideth in Christ, who doth Sacramentally eat the Flesh, and drink the Blood of Christ. A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l Unions are either <ns0:hi>Natural</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />litical Vnions.</ns0:hi> The strictest Natural Union is that of the <ns0:hi>Head</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Members</ns0:hi>; the <ns0:hi>Vine,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Branches.</ns0:hi> The strictest <ns0:hi>Political Vnion</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> is that of the <ns0:hi>Husband and Wife, Gen.</ns0:hi> 2.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. The Union betwixt Christ and a believing Soul is set out by all these, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 15.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="57">57 As the living Father <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">God is often in Holy Writ called the <ns0:hi>Living God,</ns0:hi> not only because he hath Life in himself, but because he is the Foun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>n of Life to all his Creatures. Christ here declareth his Father to be the <ns0:hi>Living Father</ns0:hi> upon the latter account, as he is the Author and Fountain of all Life;</ns0:note> hath sent me, and I <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>for the Father.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> live by the Father <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>and I live by the Father</ns0:hi> (saith he.) Some translate it <ns0:hi>for the Father</ns0:hi>; as indeed the Pr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>position <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, joyned with an Accusative Case (as it is here) doth most ordinarily signifie; but not always e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ther in Profane Authors, or in the Dialect of Scripture, as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 2.4. and 12.24. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 4.41, 42. It seemeth here (as in tho<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e Texts) to denote not so much the <ns0:hi>final</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>efficient cause</ns0:hi>; and so better Translated <ns0:hi>by,</ns0:hi> than <ns0:hi>for the Father</ns0:hi>: For Christ in this Text seems to be giving his Hearers an account how he came to be <ns0:hi>living bread</ns0:hi>; and to be in a capacity of giving Life to the World. Saith he, <ns0:hi>I live</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> who by an Eternal Generation hath communicated to me all that Life which is in him; and hath also communicated to me a quickning Power, as I am Mediator, and sent by the Father into the World, to g<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e life unto the World: Now look as I have life in my self from him who is the Fountain of Life, so</ns0:note>: so he that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ateth me, even he shall live by me <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">according to the Fathers O<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>dination, he t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>at <ns0:hi>eateth me</ns0:hi> (that is) by a true Faith, receiveth and closeth with me, as Mediator, he <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hall by me live both Spiritually and Eternally.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="58">58 This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat Manna and are dead <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">There is no more said in this Verse, than <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 49, 50, 51. See the Notes on those Verses. From this whole Dis<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ourse it is as evident as the Light, That the Justification of the Soul dependeth upon believing; and the Spiritual life of the Soul floweth not fro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>love</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>obedience</ns0:hi> to the works of the Law, but from <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in Jesus Christ: Tho it be true, that true Faith cannot be without works, and no man with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out Obedience in sincerity (tho not in perfection) to the will of God, shall ever obtain Eternal Life and Salvation; but this <ns0:hi>Obedience</ns0:hi> is not Faith, nor doth it enter into the Justification of the Soul, but is the certain and necessary product of that Faith which justifieth, which cannot be justified as true and saving, without Obedience. In all this Discourse here is no mention of Love, or Obedience, as that to which the promises of Life Everlasting, and a joy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Resurrection are so often made; but only of <ns0:hi>eating Christ, eating his Flesh, and drinking his Blood: Eating him as the bread which came down from Heaven,</ns0:hi> &c. which are Phrases no way expressive of <ns0:hi>Obedience</ns0:hi> to the works of the Law, but of <ns0:hi>believing, v.</ns0:hi> 47, 48, 49. The other Texts of Scripture make it plain enough, that there can be no believing without obeying; nor any Eternal Life and Salvation obtained without both.</ns0:note>: He that eateth of this bread, shall live for ever.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="59">59 These things said he in the Synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Tho the state of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Church at this time was Corrupt enough, both as to matters of Doctrine, Worship, and Discipline; yet it being Constituted by his Father, he did not decline their <ns0:hi>Assemblies</ns0:hi> either in the <ns0:hi>Temple at Hierusalem,</ns0:hi> or in the places of the Publick Worship, which were called <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> and were both in their Cities and Villages; for he had a liberty to teach in them, as ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peareth both from this and many other Texts; which he accordingly used, and usually spent the Sabbath, or a great part of it, in those places and Assemblies; yet by his Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sence he no way owned or declared his Approbation of their Corruptions, but frequently, and freely reproved them, onely because of those Superstitious impertinencies (there being at this time no Idolatry practised amongst them) he would not disown what was of God his Father among them: The same Practice we shall observe amongst the Apostles, till the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> declared themselves <ns0:hi>hardned,</ns0:hi> drave them out from their Synagogues, and spake evil of the <ns0:hi>way of the Gospel before the multitude,</ns0:hi> Acts 19.9. Then indeed, and not before, <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> separated the Disciples, dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />puting daily in the School of one <ns0:hi>Tyrannus.</ns0:hi> This also is further to be observed in the Practice of our Saviour, That altho he went to the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> and there joyned with the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Worship Instituted by his Father; and reproved (as he had occasion) the Corruptions they had introduced and super-added; yet he did not forbear himself Teaching the Gospel in other places besides the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Synagogues.</ns0:hi> The Evangelist also noteth, that the <ns0:hi>Synagogue</ns0:hi> where he taught these things, was in <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pernaum,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>City of Galilee,</ns0:hi> which in this was <ns0:hi>exalted to Heaven</ns0:hi>; that it had not onely the Gospel Preached in it, but by Christ himself; but for the contempt of the Gospel is since <ns0:hi>brought down to Hell</ns0:hi>; as much debased as it was before exalted, being long since reduced to a poor incon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siderable place, and at this day under the <ns0:hi>Tyranny</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Mahumetan Prince.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="60">60 Many therefore of his disciples <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">His followers, not those that were his Disciples indeed, but in name; for many followed him that did not believe in him; and many (in a sense) <ns0:hi>believed</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to whom he did not commit himself, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.23, 24. Now, many of these Disciples, having heard these sayings, and being no way able to comprehend so great Mysteries, nor having their Eyes opened by the Spirit of Illumination, said within them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />se<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ves,</ns0:note>, when they had heard <ns0:hi>this,</ns0:hi> said, This is an hard saying, who can hear it <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">These are sayings hard, or impossible to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood, who is able to hear, or to understand them? O<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> who is able to bear them?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="61">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:342" />61 When Jesus knew in himself, that his disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples murmured at it <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Christ, tho cloathed with our Flesh, yet being also the Eternal Son of God, knew by vertue o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> his Divine Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, personally United to the Humane Nature, what was in the Heart of Man; hence is this Phrase, <ns0:hi>knew in himself</ns0:hi>; which is opposed to a knowledge either from the hearing of his own Ears, as man heareth; whether more immediately from the sound of their words (for we read of nothing they spake audibly) or from the relation of others, as what they had heard; he knew in himself their thoughts by his Divine Prerogative and Property of searching the Hearts, and trying the Reins, and discerning the Thoughts of men afar off.</ns0:note>, he said unto them, Doth this offend you <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Knowing their thoughts, he saith, Doth this give you occasion of stumbling?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="62">62 <ns0:hi>What</ns0:hi> and if ye shall see the Son of man as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cend up <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.13. Acts 1.9. Ephs. 4.8.</ns0:note> where he was before <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Our Saviour by these words may seem rather to increase than to abate their Offence: That which stumbled them was, his calling himself the <ns0:hi>bread of Life</ns0:hi>; his affirming, <ns0:hi>That he came down from Heaven,</ns0:hi> That he <ns0:hi>gave life to the World</ns0:hi>; That the way to obtain this Life, was eating his Flesh, and drinking his Blood: How doth what he now tells them, any way tend to satisfie them? He now speaks of <ns0:hi>ascending up to Heaven,</ns0:hi> and asserteth <ns0:hi>that he</ns0:hi> was there before. <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> The former assertions were no way to be justified, but upon this Foundation; That tho he appeared now in the form and shape of a man, and was indeed the Son of man, yet he was also God, the Eternal Son of God; he therefore here plainly asserts that, that he was in Heaven before he appeared as the Son of man upon the Earth; and descending from thence, did assume the form of a Servant; and for a further Proof of this, he referreth them to what they were to see or hear (to know) within some few Months after this Discourse (for this was after his <ns0:hi>third Passover,</ns0:hi> which was to be the last year of his Life) <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That he should ascend up to Heaven, which it is very pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bable that some of them did see with their Bodily Eyes; for he was in <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> when he ascended, and <ns0:hi>Capernaum</ns0:hi> was a City of that <ns0:hi>Province</ns0:hi>; and when he ascended, the men of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> stood gazing up to Heaven after him, as appears from <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.11. and had a Revelation, that they should see him so come again, and descend from Heaven as they had seen him go up.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="63">63 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 3.6.</ns0:note> It is the Spirit that quickneth <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">As it is not the Bread or Flesh that a man eateth for the sustenance of his Animal or Natural Life, that doth the main work, but the Soul of a man within him; which putteth forth its Vertues and Powers in causing the Dige<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stion, Concoction, and alteration of it; without which it nourisheth not the Body:</ns0:note>, the flesh profiteth nothing <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">So the Flesh of Christ eaten Carnally, can be of no profit for the Nourishment of the Soul; nor can the Flesh of Christ considered alone, or by any Vertue in it, profit, it onely profiteth by Vertue of the <ns0:hi>Divine Nature,</ns0:hi> which being Personally United to the Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane Nature, addeth all the Vertue and Merit to the Suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferings and Actions of the Humane Nature; so as the Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane Nature of Christ hath all its quickning Vertue from the Divine Nature. It is not therefore the Carnal eating of my Flesh that I intended, that is a very gross conception of yours; nor can any such thing as that do you good: But the words that I speak to you they are Spiritual, and such, by the belief of which you may obtain a Spiritual and Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Life: For by believing those words, and obeying them, you shall come to believe in me, which is that eating my Flesh, and drinking my Blood which I intended; not any Corporeal or Carnal eating.</ns0:note>: the words that I speak unto you, <ns0:hi>they</ns0:hi> are spirit, and <ns0:hi>they</ns0:hi> are life <ns0:hi>b.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="64">64 But there are some of you that believe not <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">I may say what I will to you; the Spirit quickneth, but it doth not quicken all; it onely quickneth whomsoever it pleaseth. You understand not these things, but have most gross Conceptions of sublime Spiritual things; the reason is, because you believe not; tho some of them que<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stionless did truly believe, yet the most did not; for we read, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 66. That many of them <ns0:hi>went back, and walked</ns0:hi> no more with him.</ns0:note>. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 2.24, 25. and 13.11.</ns0:note> Jesus knew from the beginning, who they were that believed not, and who should betray him <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">And though Faith be an inward Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cret act of the Soul, yet Christ knew, and from the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning, who were Believers, and who were not; nay, he had a particular knowledge of that Disciple who was to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tray him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="65">65 And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it be given unto him of my Father <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">He said this, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 44. See the Notes on that Verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="66">66 ¶ From that <ns0:hi>time</ns0:hi> many of his disciples went back <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">His Disciples at large, so called, because they followed him, partly to hear what he would say, partly to see his Miracles,</ns0:note>, and walked no more with him <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">followed him no more: Many Professors and seeming Disciples of Christ, may draw back and fall fr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>m their Profession, tho none that truly receive Christ <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ll fall away, but he by the Power of God preserved through Faith unto Salvation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="67">67 Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">It is probable that some stayed besides the twelve; for it is said onely that <ns0:hi>many of his Disciples turned back.</ns0:hi> Nor was our Saviour (who knew the Hearts of all) ignorant what they would do; but he had a mind both to try them by this Question, and also to convince them that there was a false Brother amongst them, whose wickedness (tho it lay hid from them) would in a short time discover it self.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="68">68 Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Acts 5.20.</ns0:note> the words of eternal life <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> who is observed in the whole History of the Gospel to have discovered the hottest and quickest Spirit, and to have been first in answering Questions propounded to the twelve, as <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 16.16, &c. Replies, <ns0:hi>Lord, whi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>her shall we go, &c</ns0:hi>? thereby teaching us under Temptations to Apostacy, first, to consider what we shall get by it, as the following words teach us, that an abiding with Christ in a steady adherence to the truths of his Gospel, is the best choice that we can make.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="69">69 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 11.27.</ns0:note> And we believe, and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>We believe</ns0:hi> (saith <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi>) and are sure, both from what we have heard from thee, and from the Miracles which we have seen wrought by thee, <ns0:hi>that thou ar<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> the Christ, the Son of the living God.</ns0:hi> The very words by which St. <ns0:hi>Matthew, Chap.</ns0:hi> 16.16. expresseth that noble Confession of his, which our Saviour calleth <ns0:hi>the Rock, up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on which he would build his Church.</ns0:hi> But notwithstanding this acknowledgment, which speaks the <ns0:hi>Seeds of this F<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>th</ns0:hi> now sown in the Heart of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and the Hearts of the rest; yet whoso considereth the passages of the other Evange<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lists after this, will see reason to believe, that their persua<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion as to this was but faint, till Christ by his Resurrection declared himself the Son of God with Power.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="70">70 Jesus answered them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 6.13.</ns0:note> Have I not chosen <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Chosen,</ns0:hi> not to Eternal Life; but to the great Office of an Apostle. I chose but twelve amongst you, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 10. and of those twelve one is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, an <ns0:hi>Accuser,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />former</ns0:hi>; a name by which the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> (who is the Grand Accuser of the Brethren) is ordinarily expressed in Holy Writ.</ns0:note> you twelve, and one of you is a Devil <ns0:hi>m</ns0:hi>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="71">71 He spake of Judas Iscariot, <ns0:hi>the son</ns0:hi> of Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">This he spake of <ns0:hi>Iudas Iscariot</ns0:hi> (so called, as most think, from the name of the City where he lived) and to distinguish him from the other <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> the Brother of <ns0:hi>Iames,</ns0:hi> who wrote the Epistle that goeth by his Name; and is a part of Holy Writ: For</ns0:note>: for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">he being one of the twelve, chosen and sent out with the rest to Preach the Gospel, and impowred by Miraculous Operations to confirm the truth of it; yet it was he that was to betray Christ, as we largely read in all the Evangelists relation of the Passion. To teach us, That no Office to which God calleth us, no Gifts (except those of Special Grace) with which God blesseth any man, can secure him of an Eternal happy state; nothing can do that but a true saving Faith in Jesus Christ, with the Obedience of an Holy Life becoming the Gospel of Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
            </ns0:div>
